title: LinkedIn Is Testing a Feature That Lets You See Your Profile Stalkers
gist: LinkedIn is testing a 'Frequent Viewer' tag for some Premium users that flags people who repeatedly visit a profile; LinkedIn confirmed the test but gave no details. An early user pipes the flagged names through Claude to triage inbound opportunities, showing how the feature turns passive lurking into a lead-generation signal and pushes privacy-conscious users toward private browsing modes.

insights.claim: LinkedIn is testing a 'Frequent Viewer' tag that lets certain LinkedIn Premium subscribers see when a specific person has viewed their profile multiple times; LinkedIn confirmed the test but declined to share details.
insights.speaker: Kate Taylor
insights.so_what: A new Premium-only insight is a lever to lift paid conversion; watch whether it rolls out broadly.

insights.claim: LinkedIn Premium already lets paying users see a full list of every profile viewer over the previous year, and the Frequent Viewer tag adds a repeat-visit signal on top of that paywalled data.
insights.speaker: Kate Taylor
insights.so_what: Shows LinkedIn monetizes profile-view data as a core Premium differentiator.

insights.claim: The LinkedIn Frequent Viewer tag is triggered by direct profile visits rather than seeing a user's posts in a feed or search results, making it a stronger intent signal that someone is specifically seeking that person out.
insights.speaker: Kate Taylor
insights.so_what: Higher-intent signals raise the value of LinkedIn data for sales and recruiting workflows.

insights.claim: Agency founder Krista Mollion, who has about 79,000 LinkedIn followers, runs her LinkedIn frequent viewers through Anthropic's Claude, which sorts them into friends, likely sellers, and business development or sales leads.

insights.so_what: Example of consumer LLMs being bolted onto platform data for lightweight CRM-style triage.

insights.claim: LinkedIn's Frequent Viewer tag also exposes unwanted repeat visitors such as former bosses or exes, and users seeking to avoid detection can switch to semi-private or fully private profile-viewing mode.

insights.so_what: Visibility features can backfire on browsing volume if users shift to private mode; watch engagement effects.
